details: US President Donald Trump issued an executive order under the new Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, waiving tariffs and many sanctions but raising duties on Russian goods by 500% and imposing additional 100% duties on major importers of Russian oil and gas making new purchases from October 18. EU leaders expressed regret, reaffirming support for Ukraine and urging stronger measures against hybrid threats. The move comes as US Representative Gregory Meeks introduced legislation to block the Trump administration from importing Russian diesel. Meanwhile, transit through the Strait of Hormuz remains about 70% below pre-conflict levels due to ongoing attacks, with 12 vessel attacks reported in the last week by a UK maritime agency.
title: Trump Waives Some Russia Sanctions Amid EU Pushback on Diesel Deal

details: Iran has publicly stated it will respond "immediately" to any US threats directed at its energy facilities. This announcement escalates tensions in the Middle East, a region already experiencing instability and disruptions to oil supply chains.
title: Iran Threatens Immediate Response to US Energy Facility Threats

details: Global financial markets are showing signs of nearing a "breaking point" due to escalating conflicts in the Middle East and between the US and Ukraine, alongside a significant AI-related market sell-off. Concerns are growing that rising interest rates could create funding challenges within the increasingly complex AI ecosystem, impacting heavily indebted companies and leading to broader market unease.
title: Global Markets Face "Tipping Point" Amid Geopolitical Escalations & AI Sell-off

details: Iranians are increasingly turning to cryptocurrencies as a means to circumvent stringent US sanctions, which have led to flight cancellations and soaring costs within the country. While offering a way to move money, these methods also come with their own set of problems and risks.
title: Iranians Use Crypto to Evade US Sanctions Amid Soaring Costs

details: China's continued buying of gold is a significant trend impacting global financial markets. Concurrently, US inflation has risen ahead of midterm elections, fueling concerns about potential interest rate hikes. This economic uncertainty is contributing to a tense market environment globally.
title: China's Gold Purchases & US Inflation Drive Market Uncertainty
